option_relations.rationale: Sézary Syndrome is a distinct type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, characterized by erythroderma and circulating Sézary cells, which is not directly equivalent to or a subtype of classic mycosis fungoides.
Mycosis Fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) is the full name for the disease, and 'Mycosis fungoides (classic)' is a specific presentation of it, making them essentially equivalent in this context.
Adult T-cell Leukemia/Lymphoma is a distinct hematologic malignancy caused by HTLV-1, which is different from Mycosis Fungoides.
Ichthyosiform mycosis fungoides is a rare variant of mycosis fungoides, making it a subtype of the broader 'Mycosis fungoides (classic)'.
